name: Compliant Naira
oneLiner: cNGN is a centralized Nigerian naira stablecoin backed 1:1 by NGN deposits at designated Nigerian commercial banks under the cNGN issuer consortium.
collateral: Nigerian naira reserves held 1:1 in designated commercial bank accounts by the cNGN issuer consortium
pegMechanism: Issuer-managed mint and redemption path designed to maintain 1 cNGN = 1 NGN through naira reserves and compliant transfer rails

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Explicit Yes retained: centralized governance metadata indicates issuer or admin control; registry links were reviewed for direct freeze, blacklist, pause, burn, or upgrade authority.

mintAuthority.summary: cNGN is issued by WrappedCBDC Ltd under the Africa Stablecoin Consortium and SEC Nigeria oversight; tokens are minted by the consortium treasury through a multi-party-authorized mint request after naira is deposited at partner banks, and burned on redemption.

controls.label: Africa Stablecoin Consortium issuance backend (multi-party authorized)
controls.evidence: Mint requests require treasury verification of the naira deposit plus approval by several authorized staff before tokens are created; burn occurs on redemption. Authorized exchange partners can also mint/burn against consortium reserves. Supply is fully issuer/consortium-controlled with no permissionless route.

review.evidence: cNGN coverage and issuer materials describe a fully reserved consortium mint-and-burn with multi-party authorization tied to naira bank deposits across its multi-chain deployments; no user-collateralized or permissionless mint exists.
review.sourceFreeRationale: Classification based on consortium issuer model in project materials/coverage; the on-chain minter/owner admin on each chain (and the Solana mint authority) was not independently resolved.
unresolvedQuestions: Resolve the on-chain minter/owner admin per chain and the Solana SPL mint authority for cNGN before raising confidence.

reserves.name: Nigerian naira deposits at designated commercial banks
